david: noticing p99 spikes on GPU pool A since yesterday evening. baseline p50 ~80ms but p99 jumps to 1.6s for a subset of requests.

molly: oof. any correlation with model variant or sequence length?

david: early signal points to three things: long prompts (>4k tokens), requests that trigger tool-calling loops, and some requests hitting a kernel-fallback path that adds ~600ms. attached a short profile.

kai: can you paste the stack/profile?

david: sure — CPU/GPU timeline excerpt:
```
GPU0: kernel_flash_attn (fast) -> 42ms
GPU0: kernel_fallback_matmul -> 638ms  (fp32 fallback, allocs)
KV cache: miss on prefix for ~12% of p99 requests -> replay from disk
Batching: microbatch=8, burst wait=15ms
External call: toolbot lookup -> avg 120ms but sometimes blocks 900ms
```

ana: two separate issues: kernel fallback + tool call tail. both can amplify each other when batching groups a long prompt with a short one.

molly: is the fallback due to unsupported sequence length or quantization mismatch?

david: kernel logs show "no optimized kernel for seq_len=4096, fallback to gemm". looks like our kernel selector is conservative for >2k. commit 1f7b2b changed selector thresholds last week.

kai: ah — that commit was to avoid OOM on some A100 80G configs. maybe regression. can we reproduce with a tiny script?

david: pushing repro in a minute. repro steps: send mixed-length batch (one 512, one 4096), microbatching enabled=on, kernel selector should pick flash for both but falls back for the long one.

infra-bot: canary deployed: runtime/selector-fix v2026.3.10 -> cluster A (3 nodes) at 1752104400

molly: good. but tool-call loops still scary. we logged traces where model emits a function call, tool returns a long JSON, model re-enters tool-call because of partial parsing -> loop. that's a tail latency multiplicative effect.

kai: two mitigation tracks: 1) kernel selector tune to expand flash/kernel coverage for long seqs (needs perf regression check), 2) batching heuristic change to avoid co-batching long+short (prefer same-length grouping) and set microbatch cap.

ana: also add per-request tool timeout and detect repeated tool calls within a single generation, cap to N attempts. that will bound worst-case.

molly: profiling suggests microbatch=8 was chosen to maximize throughput but p99 suffers. try microbatch=2 or dynamic microbatch that biases for latency SLO. we can run A/B on canary.

kai: agreed. i'll roll a test: 1) microbatch=2, prefer-length-grouping, 2) selector revert to previous threshold, 3) tool timeout=500ms + max_tool_calls=2. run for 4h and compare p50/p95/p99.

david: logs to watch: `kernel_fallback_count`, `kv_replay_hits`, `tool_call_retries`, `batch_size_distribution`. I'll add dashboards.

molly: one more: KV cache behavior — we saw "prefix eviction" for long prefix requests causing re-compute of past tokens. maybe our KV LRU is using allocation size, not token count. leads to small long sessions evicting many short ones.

ana: simple fix: change eviction to token-weighted LRU and preserve last N tokens per session. low-risk patch.

kai: timeline: I'll push canary changes by EOD, run 4h A/B, collect traces and a perf regression job to ensure no throughput drop >7% on standard workloads.

david: assigning owners: kai (selector + batching), ana (KV cache), molly (tool-call protection + dashboards). I'll create the PRs and link here.

molly: thanks — tagging @here for visibility. any quick wins we can ship immediately? the tool timeout + max calls is small change, and KV eviction tweak seems safe.

deploy-bot: PR merged: infra/kv-evict-tokenweight (#4523) at 1752104520

kai: starting canary now. will post results in ~4h. pre-check: capturing traces with sampling=100% for p99 flows.

david: awesome. if p99 still spikes after this, next steps are to add per-request CPU/GPU preemption and move long prompts to a slower lower-cost pool to avoid impacting latency SLO.

molly: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
